newsitem.title: ALBANIA: SOCCER-ALBANIA TO RESUME INTERRUPTED SOCCER CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ALBANIA TO RESUME INTERRUPTED SOCCER CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: The 1996-97 Albanian soccer league season which was suspended after 17 matches in early February because of civil unrest, will resume next month.

The remaining five fixtures will all be played in a two-week spell between August 2-16 and all matches will be played on neutral grounds. Although the league was formally suspended in February, no matches have been played in the competition since December 29.
The 1997-98 season will start on September 13.
Albanian F.A. spokesman Besnik Cela said the 18 first division teams would split into three groups according to the points they have already gained.

The selected venues are government-controlled towns in western and central Albania which have been relatively safe, unlike the south of the country where bandits roam freely following the outbreak of civil unrest earlier this year.
The championship is starting after the holding of general elections which gave a landslide victory to the ex-communist Socialist Party.

Flamurtari from the southern port town of Vlore where the revolt against collapsed pyramid schemes started, leads the table with 37 points, followed by Tirana on 34 and Vllaznia on 33. Although there are signs that soccer is returning to normal in the Balkan state, the national side will still be playing their final World Cup Group Nine home qualifier against Northern Ireland on September 10 in Spain.
Albanian clubs however, remain suspended by UEFA from taking part in European competitions for the coming season.
